messages:
maya: Hi—trying to track down a request that errors in prod but I can't find any logs for the request_id. Seen this before?

owen: what request_id / trace_id? sometimes console sampling hides things or it got routed through the edge and lost x-req-id header.

maya: request_id=9c3b7a2f, trace_id=00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01. I queried the requests dashboard but it shows no matching log lines.

liam: quick checklist: 1) console sampling/ingest level 2) check proxy/nginx logs 3) check edge/region proxy 4) look for span links in traces. I usually run stern on the proxy pods.

maya: ok trying stern.

maya: ```bash
stern -n infra-proxy -l app=proxy "9c3b7a2f|9c3b7a2f" --since 1h
```

owen: FYI the proxy uses header `x-rw-reqid` not `x-req-id` in some older clusters. If the header was dropped, trace->reqid mapping will be missing. Check proxy access logs for the upstream id.

liam: if stern doesn't show it, grep logs from the last hour across nodes: ```bash
kubectl logs -n infra-proxy -l app=proxy --since=1h | rg "9c3b7a2f" -n
```

maya: stern returned nothing. kubectl grep also empty. 

owen: next: check the edge LB logs (nginx on gateway). You can query cloud logs: `gcloud logging read` or via the console dashboard. Example: 
```bash
gcloud logging read 'jsonPayload.requestId="9c3b7a2f"' --project=redwood-prod --limit=50
```

maya: ran the gcloud query, edge logs show entries but they have only trace_id, no request_id. They do include upstream IP and user-agent.

liam: try correlating by trace_id instead. Console traces page -> search for that trace id, then follow the span that hits our proxy and note the span tags (req header). Sometimes the request_id is in a span tag called `rw.req_id` or `http.request.header.x-rw-reqid`.

maya: I can find the trace. The proxy span metadata has `http.request.header.x-rw-reqid: (missing)` but there's `edge.request_id: e-112233`.

owen: aha — that edge.request_id is generated by the gateway and not propagated. We have a helper script that maps edge ids to internal req ids via trace sampling. Try this quick script: 
```bash
# pulls spans for a trace and prints candidate req headers
python tools/trace_helpers/get_headers_for_trace.py --trace 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736
```

maya: running it now...

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new rollout completed for infra-proxy v2.14.0 :rocket: (no restarts in last 5m)

maya: script found an internal header `x-internal-req: 9c3b7a2f` attached to the app-span, but it wasn't written to stdout because the app crashed before flush.

liam: that explains missing console logs — app crashed very early and stderr didn't flush to structured logs. Check pod kube events for OOM or container exit around the timestamp (2112345678 -> convert to human).

maya: pod shows `OOMKilled` at roughly the same time. How do I pull the terminated container logs?

owen: use `kubectl logs --previous` on the pod. If pods rotated, find prior pod by `kubectl get pods --show-all -n app` or look up replicaset events. Example: 
```bash
kubectl logs -n my-app <pod-name> --previous | rg "9c3b7a2f"
```

maya: got it — previous container logs show the request lifecycle up to the crash and the internal header present. Lines: `internal-req=9c3b7a2f lat=54ms err="panic: nil pointer"`

sanya: nice find. Next steps: 1) add guard so crash logs flush, 2) add a small sync on panic path, 3) add span tag for `x-rw-reqid` earlier in pipeline so console can link. Could also set ingress to copy edge.request_id -> x-rw-reqid.

maya: will open a tiny PR for panic flush and add a follow-up ticket to propagate header.

liam: for posterity, add a short note in the requests dashboard doc about `how to chase when request_id missing` and include the commands we used.

maya: will add steps + the `get_headers_for_trace.py` usage. Thanks! :pray:
